#220 correctness review, round 2: PASS

Exact head: `59a35cdc15271eeffc5dab63c5178c53ec108ebd`. Scoped to the repairs since `0eb43f285c5ede32ceccc232f7f23a6c150df23b`, final round under C34.

**F001 closed:** direct admission and the memory-turn continuation now share `lifecycle::may_close`. The continuation re-evaluates designation and dead-orphan eligibility against the current row, while retaining the existing revived-incarnation and reparenting brakes. The new role-holding orphan regression exercises held admission through completed close.

**F002 / S220-001 closed:** another live record on the pane now vetoes `Own` before timestamp compatibility is considered. The inverted unit case and HTTP predecessor/successor case cover the shared-process/shared-pane situation. This is a one-direction safety brake: withholding a conflicting kill hint cannot authorize additional teardown. The other holder's name also goes through the seat renderer.

The new `pane_process_without_launch` uses only `query_live`; a cold/unavailable control client remains unchecked and names no concrete kill command. A failed or malformed read, including the empty fields tmux returns for a nonexistent target in control mode, is distinguished using the launch-free live pane list. The real-tmux regression checks cold/disabled/live/missing-pane cases and verifies no added launch.

**Evidence:** `just pr-freeze 220` returned FINAL at this head; detached tree clean. [CI run 42766504026](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42766504026) records the exact head. Its successful Rust job's [JUnit artifact 13740111587](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42766504026/artifacts/13740111587) contains 2,419 executed tests, zero failures/errors; nextest reports six additional skips. The held-prime close, competing-holder HTTP/classifier, real-control no-launch and retained revived/reparented-seat cases ran and passed.

No new periodic work or launch site. Source and exact-head CI evidence only; no local builds/tests, close/reap/kill commands, lifecycle mutations or product edits.
